transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-21 16:21 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Evan Li (Redwood), Jordan Park (Zenith Head of ML), Maya Rodriguez (Platform), Samir Patel (CTO), Clara Nguyen (Security)

Summary:
Quick technical demo and parity mapping workshop focused on moving Zenith's multi-vendor stack (OpenAI chat + Anthropic assistant + Together long-form) to Redwood API with equivalent latency and cost targets. Discussed staging pilot, perf benchmarks, caching/kv strategies, SSO/KMS, and next steps for a two-week pilot.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and pain points: cost variability, regional residency, cold-starts
- Parity mapping: model equivalents, prompt tweaks, sampling/temperature differences
- Integration: API surface, streaming, tool-calls, function calling gaps
- Ops: batching, KV cache, quantization, dedicated pools vs hosted fallback
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, data retention
- Pilot plan and success criteria: latency P95 < 450ms for chat small requests, embedding parity within 2% accuracy, cost delta < 30%

Transcript:
00:00:03 Alex Moreno: hey everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Alex with Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, we've got priya our se and evan here. how's everyone doing?
00:00:10 Jordan Park: good, uh thanks, we wanted to keep this focused — compatibility mapping and a plan to run a real pilot so we can answer our execs questions on latency and cost.
00:00:21 Maya Rodriguez: hi all, from infra perspective we need to understand auth flows and how to do private vpc egress, and also encryption at rest.
00:00:30 Priya Shah: great, we'll walk through the console, the api parity surface and then dig into batching/kv cache and quantization suggestions. quick ask — can you remind us of your current traffic profile, maya?
00:00:42 Maya Rodriguez: sure, so bursty, roughly 40 rps average across our endpoints, peaks to 280 rps during day, tail is long requests for generation — about 8% of calls are >2k tokens. embedding traffic is steady, around 1k qps but small vectors.
00:01:00 Priya Shah: ok that helps, sounds like you'll benefit from dedicated pools for steady embedding throughput and hosted nodes for bursty chat unless you want full private deployment.
00:01:08 Samir Patel: we want to avoid full on-prem unless we have to — compliance-heavy clients will demand it but for now VPC/private plane might be fine. two asks: native sso and proof of key management integration.
00:01:22 Clara Nguyen: yeah, and audit logs that show per-token redaction — we need to be able to show auditors what was persisted and what was not.
00:01:29 Priya Shah: absolutely, Redwood supports SSO/SAML and KMS pairing; we can show a redacted audit log example as part of the security pack.
00:01:36 Alex Moreno: alright we will show the console — first quick parity table: "OpenAI gpt-4o" -> Redwood equivalent is our curated 4x:red-4o-sim, Anthropic Claude -> red-safety-claude-compat, Together long-form -> redlong-optim, roughly. note those are names for demo not exact.
00:01:56 Jordan Park: sorry, question — how much prompt rework is typically required? we have a lot of templated system messages and tool-calling patterns.
00:02:05 Priya Shah: good question. usually small adjustments: tokenization differences and stop token handling, temperature mapping. function-calling support is matching but the json schema enforcement is slightly stricter on Redwood runtime, so one or two validations. we include a prompt delta report as part of pilot.
00:02:22 Evan Li: also worth calling out kv cache semantics — if you use prefix caching on Redwood we can reduce repeated context cost significantly with no code changes in most cases. we can show example with your three canonical prompts.
00:02:35 Maya Rodriguez: that sounds promising, how does the kv cache interact with privacy? we can't leak user data across tenants.
00:02:41 Priya Shah: kv is per-customer and per-deployment — it's isolated. for Private deployments you control the keys. on Hosted we encrypt at rest with customer-managed keys if needed.
00:02:53 Jordan Park: can you walk through a short demo of the API call side-by-side versus OpenAI?
00:02:58 Priya Shah: yep, i'll share my screen — apologies if transcription loses some words. so here is the standard request: we accept the same conversational frames, streaming, delta attachments. the primary difference is model field names and a few extra operators for routing and cost-optimization.
00:03:18 (screen share noise)
00:03:45 Priya Shah: example: openai client call -> model: "gpt-4o"; on redwood it's model: "red-4o-sim". same messages array, same max_tokens param, but we have an optional "route_policy" field so you can prefer low-latency region or low-cost fallback.
00:04:05 Jordan Park: how do fallbacks work when a model is unavailable mid-request? we have strict latency slos for chat.
00:04:12 Priya Shah: for streaming generation we prefer to return a compatible fallback model immediately; if the primary model can't satisfy the SLO we reroute to the fallback and we emit structured metadata so you can detect quality regressions and trigger re-try logic.
00:04:28 Maya Rodriguez: ok and how about batching, we're concerned about latency for small requests — we can't batch everything.
00:04:34 Evan Li: Redwood has workload aware batching; small, latency-sensitive calls are routed to low-latency nodes with minimal batching windows; higher throughput paths batch more aggressively. you can tune per-route in the console.
00:04:49 Jordan Park: real talk: cost — we've been quoted double the cost on a hosted offering elsewhere versus openai's list. can you give us rough numbers?
00:04:58 Alex Moreno: we will send detailed pricing but for a pilot we can show three scenarios: hosted with autoscale, dedicated reserved capacity, and private on prem. Typical customers see 20-35% unit cost savings from better batching and caching; quantization can further reduce infra cost on dedicated.
00:05:15 Samir Patel: quantization — do you support int8/llm-int8 or are you recommending 4-bit quant?
00:05:21 Priya Shah: Both paths are supported. For production we often recommend 8-bit or 4-bit QLoRA depending on model and workload. Redwood Optimize will recommend profiles from your sample workload.
00:05:33 Clara Nguyen: security detail — who manages keys for hosted? do you support customer-managed keys in KMS?
00:05:38 Alex Moreno: yes, customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM for private. we'll surface key rotation policies and logs.
00:05:46 Maya Rodriguez: excellent. next can we talk about embeddings parity? our semantic search relies on OpenAI-embedding-ada similarity characteristics.
00:05:55 Priya Shah: embeddings mapping is one of the easier parity items. we have curated embedding families and similarity calibration tools; customers typically run a small re-embedding experiment across a sample corpus and we measure recall/drop. target is within 1-3% for top-k recall.
00:06:10 Jordan Park: how long does a re-embedding job take? we have ~120M documents.
00:06:16 Evan Li: for 120M at 1k qps you can expect a couple weeks if you run dedicated pools; we can parallelize and provide a roadmap that uses live dual-reads during migration to avoid downtime.
00:06:28 Jordan Park: dual-read pattern — can you explain?
00:06:31 Priya Shah: sure — during migration you write embeddings to both systems and read from new system for a shadow period; if recall drops you fallback to original for some queries. it's operational but minimizes risk.
00:06:43 (brief crosstalk)
00:07:00 Alex Moreno: switching gears to pilot specifics — we're proposing two-week pilot: week 1 ingest and calibration, week 2 live shadow traffic at 10-20% with P95 tracking. success metrics: P95 latency under 450ms for short chat, embedding recall within 2% top-5, cost delta under 30%.
00:07:21 Samir Patel: that aligns with exec asks. what's the uplift in infra needed to hit your P95 targets?
00:07:27 Priya Shah: depends on token mix; from your histogram i'd recommend a dedicated embedding pool (N GPUs) and a small dedicated chat pool with autoscale for bursts — we can simulate with the bench harness and give exact GPU counts for the pilot.
00:07:40 Maya Rodriguez: bench harness — can we plug our harness in or do you provide one?
00:07:44 Evan Li: we provide a harness but it's also compatible with Locust/jmeter. we can take your existing harness and run it against our endpoints with a compat shim.
00:07:52 Jordan Park: great, any gotchas when moving tool-calls? we rely on a bunch of internal microservices via function calling.
00:07:59 Priya Shah: function calling is supported; some semantics around partial completion and structured output differ slightly and we recommend schema validation at your side. we can help with a set of best-practices in the pilot.
00:08:12 Clara Nguyen: on audit logs — can you show an example redacted log?
00:08:17 Priya Shah: yes, i'll drop a sample in the security pack — we'll obfuscate PII and show per-request metadata (model used, tokens, region, route policy).
00:08:26 Alex Moreno: ok quick pause — any other blockers?
00:08:29 Speaker 1: um yes, licensing — if we do dedicated reserved, what's the minimum commitment?
00:08:35 Alex Moreno: commitments vary; we'll propose a 3 month minimum for pilot-to-prod transition and annual for full reserved. i'll send the pricing bands in the spreadsheet.
00:08:43 (10 minute demo of console omitted — noisy transcription)
00:18:50 Priya Shah: now walking through optimize recommendations: from sample traffic we can suggest batching windows, quant profiles and a cache policy. these are suggestions and you can lock or override them per-route.
00:19:05 Jordan Park: how automated is that? can it be included in a CI pipeline?
00:19:09 Evan Li: the recommendations are API-first — we produce a config dif that you can apply; you can also pin settings per-deployment and rollout via console.
00:19:18 Maya Rodriguez: we'd want a safe rollback, so can we canary changes?
00:19:21 Priya Shah: yes, rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic fallback policies if quality metrics degrade.
00:19:30 Jordan Park: any customers that did this with similar scale?
00:19:33 Alex Moreno: a couple — one was a commerce search provider at similar size, they cut token cost by 28% during steady-state. happy to connect you with references after NDA.
00:19:43 Clara Nguyen: quick compliance question: do you have SOC2 Type II?
00:19:47 Alex Moreno: yes, we do — we'll include the report in the security pack.
00:19:51 Jordan Park: ok, let's talk about timeline — we need a pilot before end of november to inform decision in december.
00:19:58 Priya Shah: that's feasible. provisioning the pilot infra takes 48-72 hours once we have a PO or trial OK and a contact for auth.
00:20:08 Maya Rodriguez: auth — we use SAML with Okta. any issues?
00:20:12 Priya Shah: no, SAML + SCIM is standard. we'll need an Okta admin to set up and we can integrate with organization provisioning.
00:20:19 Jordan Park: in terms of integration work — estimate dev effort? we have a small infra team.
00:20:23 Alex Moreno: initial integration for api-level calls is low effort, 1-2 engineers for a week to wire up auth, dual-read, and small prompt tweaks. if you want on-prem it's longer.
00:20:34 Samir Patel: what's the fallout if a model variant causes a response change — do you have evals for regressions?
00:20:40 Priya Shah: Redwood has eval hooks in the console; we can tie regression alerts to prompt sets and notify via webhook. for pilot we'll define guardrails.
00:20:50 Jordan Park: can you give an example of a prompt delta report?
00:20:54 Priya Shah: yes, we do a token-level diff and example output comparison on the sample prompts — we'll highlight any semantic drift and suggested prompt patches.
00:21:05 Alex Moreno: ok, time for a quick Q and A and then recap.
00:21:10 Jordan Park: will you run a synthetic benchmark against our real prompt set or do we need to sanitize?
00:21:15 Priya Shah: we prefer sanitized canonical prompts but can sign an NDA for a small snippet. best practice is to provide representative prompts with redaction and we run the bench harness.
00:21:26 Maya Rodriguez: storage residency — can we keep data in eu-west-1?
00:21:30 Alex Moreno: yes, region pinning is available; for Private you'll have full control.
00:21:35 Clara Nguyen: final question — how do you handle retention and purge?
00:21:39 Priya Shah: retention is configurable per deployment; we support auto-purge windows and can provide deletion certificates for compliance.
00:21:47 Alex Moreno: recap and next steps: 1) we'll share parity mapping spreadsheet and pricing bands; 2) Priya will spin up pilot endpoints and bench harness; 3) Zenith to share traffic histograms, canonical prompts and Okta admin contact; 4) Security pack will be sent with SOC2, KMS docs and redacted log sample.
00:22:10 Jordan Park: sounds good, can we get the pilot started next week?
00:22:14 Priya Shah: yes, once we have PO/trial ok and the auth contact we'll provision — i'll aim for endpoint readiness by Monday 2026-10-26.
00:22:22 Samir Patel: appreciate it, thanks.
00:22:25 Alex Moreno: awesome, thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and scheduling invite.
